nvidia-pascal.note: reference architecture — the baseline GPU (GTX 1060 6GB, §5.3) is Pascal, so this anchors BASELINE_PERF directly.

nvidia-turing.note: calibrated so RTX 2070 ~= GTX 1080 Ti (well-known 2018 launch consensus); see data/METHODOLOGY.md

nvidia-ampere.note: calibrated so RTX 3070 ~= RTX 2080 Ti (NVIDIA's own launch claim); see data/METHODOLOGY.md

nvidia-ada.note: calibrated so RTX 4070 Ti ~= RTX 3090 (commonly cited launch comparison); see data/METHODOLOGY.md

amd-rdna2.note: calibrated so RX 6900 XT ~= RTX 3080 (well-known launch rivalry); partly compensates for Infinity Cache effective bandwidth the formula doesn't model directly — see data/METHODOLOGY.md

intel-alchemist.note: calibrated so Arc A770 ~= RTX 3060 Ti (commonly cited launch comparison); consistent with Arc's well-documented weak per-FLOP gaming efficiency at launch — see data/METHODOLOGY.md

intel-skylake.note: reference architecture — the baseline CPU (Core i5-8400) is Skylake-derived (also covers Kaby Lake/Coffee Lake, near-identical per-core IPC).

amd-zen3.note: estimate: Zen3 gaming IPC widely reported roughly on par with or slightly ahead of contemporary Skylake-class parts; see data/METHODOLOGY.md

amd-zen4.note: estimate: zen3 x AMD's own ~13% claimed IPC uplift for Zen4; see data/METHODOLOGY.md

amd-piledriver.note: estimate: Bulldozer-family IPC is well-documented as far below contemporary Intel cores; low-confidence rough estimate spanning a wide generation gap — see data/METHODOLOGY.md
